papers.title: Global Regularization of the Spatial Elliptic Restricted Three-body Problem: Quaternionic, Hamiltonian Formulation
papers.abstract: Any objects in space may encounter singularity due to the inverse-square law of the gravitational force, hindering the analysis and propagation of particle motion in space. Regularization in celestial mechanics removes such gravitational singularities in equations of motion by transforming the time and coordinates. This paper addresses a class of regularization methods known as global regularization for restricted three-body problems (R3BPs), which simultaneously removes the two singularities (e.g., Earth and Moon in cislunar space). It enables analysis, propagation, and prediction of particle motion throughout the domain of R3BPs, which is in stark contrast to regularizing each singularity individually. In particular, this paper develops a formulation for global regularization of the spatial elliptic R3BP (ER3BP) under external perturbations. The presented formulation leverages mathematical tools from quaternionic (hyper-complex) algebra and Hamiltonian mechanics. This approach enables us to (i) elegantly handle the four-dimensional coordinates arising from the dimension-lifting operation for spatial regularization, (ii) systematically derive the coordinate-momentum transformation while preserving the canonical structure and incorporating perturbing forces, and (iii) provide geometric insights for analyzing the regularity of the transformation, resulting Hamiltonian, and dynamical flow. Numerical examples demonstrate the validity of the mathematical results as well as significant numerical benefits of the regularization formulation in perturbed Earth-Moon ER3BP.

papers.title: (Super-)fast convergence rates for Chernoff approximations via centered differences and Richardson extrapolation
papers.abstract: We use centered differences to construct Chernoff families and derive even asymptotic expansions for their iterated products. Richardson extrapolation is then used to cancel polynomial part and thereby raise the convergence order. As illustrations, we apply the construction to uniformly parabolic, Schr\"odinger-type second-order operators and to a third-order dispersive operator, obtaining, at extrapolation depth $m$, the rates $ O(n^{-2m}) $ on the Sobolev scales $H^{2m+\delta}$, $H^{4m}$, and $H^{5m}$, respectively, with arbitrary $\delta>0$. In the analytic category, quantitative all-order estimates allow the extrapolation depth to grow with the base resolution and yield the super-fast rates $e^{-cn^2}$ for the two second-order models and $e^{-cn} $ for the third-order model. The constructions are explicit in terms of the coefficients of the underlying differential operators and do not use the target semigroup in their definition. This provides a constructive positive answer to the challenge of super-fast Chernoff approximation formulated by Remizov in Problem 30 of arXiv:2410.00416.

papers.title: Universal set of Observables for Forecasting Physical Systems through Causal Embedding
papers.abstract: We show how a pair of points can uniquely represent a left-infinite sequence obtained from observations of an underlying dynamical system through a phenomenon called \textit{causal embedding}. A driven dynamical system creates such pairs, and a function can be learnt on them that can reconstruct the underlying dynamics as in Takens delay embedding. The approach assures embedding stability unlike Takens delay embedding, and learnability which can be absent while stability can be present in the current reservoir computing framework. This accurately models underlying systems where recent methods like the next-generation reservoir computing fail. We demonstrate results and compare with the other methods including SINDY-PI.

papers.title: Frobenius Revivals in Laplacian Cellular Automata: Replication, Entropy, and Information Recovery
papers.abstract: We investigate Frobenius revivals in prime-modulus Laplacian cellular automata. The Frobenius identity yields exact superpositions of translated, coefficient-weighted seed copies at prime-power times; we distinguish this algebraic replication from their geometric separation. We investigate seed recovery from separated replicas and evaluate the correction of independent symbol errors introduced during transmission of encoded configurations. For the diagonal neighborhood, we determine the exact periods of moving corner operators on square windows and establish sufficient conditions for recovering any binary seed under a binary--ternary--binary schedule. The results connect prime-power algebraic structure with spatial pattern formation and precisely delimited forms of information recovery.

papers.title: Prediction Limits and Koopman Closure of Geometry-Induced Soft State Abstractions
papers.abstract: Soft state representations assign states nonnegative class weights that sum to one, but agreement with reference labels does not guarantee accurate prediction of the next weight vector. We derive lower confidence bounds on the minimum population root-mean-square prediction error over linear predictors with a prescribed spectral-norm limit. The bounds compare within-class successor variation with retained within-class input variation, with an alternative based on reference-label deviation. They are estimated from independent transition pairs without fitting a prediction matrix to the evaluation data. A bound above a chosen error tolerance excludes that accuracy for every admissible predictor at the stated confidence level; a bound of zero does not establish whether an accurate predictor exists. For coordinates constructed from Kernel Affine Hull Machine reconstruction scores, we relate the reference class's affinity advantage over competitors to label agreement. The class-centered population bound equals the optimum in a four-state example. Using 117,000 previously generated evaluation datasets from fixed four-state designs, we compare the finite-sample certificates with an empirical-risk-minimization baseline. For one Van der Pol representation selected before evaluation, the label-based bound is positive in all 64 independent evaluation datasets at the fitted matrix's spectral norm. Separately, exact matrix propagation under deterministic dynamics yields a Koopman interpretation of the coordinate-function span. The certificates help identify forecasting targets that cannot be reached by refitting a fixed representation within a specified predictor class and evaluation distribution.

papers.title: Contractor Filters
papers.abstract: We introduce Contractor Filters (CFs), a set-membership architecture for nonlinear continuous-time state estimation with bounded uncertainties and sporadic outliers. CFs represent feasible states symbolically by compositions of contractors rather than rematerializing a geometric enclosure after each update. This provides an abstraction layer between the set-theoretic filtering equations and their numerical realization, so prediction, correction, ambiguity, and outlier handling can be expressed within one algebra without prescribing a state geometry. We derive an exact nominal recursion and a guaranteed robust enclosure, with validated flow inclusions preserving soundness. Optional sub-paving compression then provides finite outer representations. CFs are evaluated against a robust particle filter on range-only and terrain-based localization under outliers, probabilistic model mismatch, association ambiguity, and multimodality. CFs retain the simulated truth in all tested configurations, while particle-filter reliability degrades under persistent bias and spatial aliasing. Contractor strength and compression budget control the trade-off between paving tightness and computational cost, while preserving the enclosure guarantee.

papers.title: An Approximate-Master-Equation Formulation of the Watts Threshold Model on Hypergraphs
papers.abstract: In traditional models of behavioral and opinion dynamics on networks, researchers suppose that interactions occur between pairs of individuals. However, in reality, social interactions also occur in sets of three or more individuals. A common way to incorporate such polyadic interactions is to study dynamical processes on hypergraphs, in which interactions can occur between any number of the individuals. A major current effort is to generalize popular dynamical processes from graphs to hypergraphs. One important model is the Watts threshold model (WTM), which describes a simplistic social spreading process and was extended recently by Chen et al. from dyadic networks (i.e., ordinary graphs) to polyadic networks (i.e., hypergraphs). In the present paper, we extend their discrete-time model to continuous time by using approximate master equations (AMEs). By employing AMEs, we are able to very accurately model the mean behavior of the continuous-time system. We reduce the high-dimensional AME system to a system of three coupled ordinary differential equations without any detectable loss of accuracy. This much lower-dimensional system is computationally faster to solve numerically, and it is also easier to interpret. We linearize the reduced AME system and derive a cascade condition, which allows us to determine when a large spreading event occurs. We then examine our reduced AME system on a contact hypergraph of a French primary school and on a hypergraph of computer-science coauthorships. We find that our full and reduced AME systems give reasonably good descriptions of the mean time-dependent fraction of active nodes in the polyadic WTM dynamics on these empirical networks.

papers.title: Lyapunov characterization of boundedness of reachability sets for infinite-dimensional systems
papers.abstract: We prove a converse Lyapunov theorem for boundedness of reachability sets for a general class of control systems whose flow is Lipschitz continuous on compact intervals with respect to trajectory-dominated inputs. We show that this condition is satisfied by broad classes of semilinear evolution equations. For ordinary differential equations, as a consequence of our results, we obtain a converse Lyapunov theorem for forward completeness, without a priori restrictions on the magnitude of inputs. As an example, we rederive Wintner's classical result using our Lyapunov approach.

papers.title: Mean-Field Oscillator Ising Machines: Gradient Flows and Classification of Limit Solutions
papers.abstract: Oscillator Ising Machines (OIMs) have emerged as promising computational architectures for approximating solutions to combinatorial optimization problems. We derive and analyze the mean-field limit of an OIM model and show that it inherits the gradient flow structure of the finite-dimensional dynamics. We identify conditions under which this mean-field evolution admits an Eulerian formulation as a gradient flow on the Wasserstein space of probability measures and contrast this with a Lagrangian formulation which is always available. This gradient flow structure strongly constrains the long-time dynamics and enables a complete classification of limit solutions and their stability in the totally symmetric case. In particular, all limit solutions are fixed points whose phases cluster into at most four groups, and for almost all parameter values, only binarized fixed points -- those with clusters at $0$ and/or $\pi$ -- can be stable. Since binarized states are exactly those for which a feasible solution to the original problem can be read out, this shows that feasible solutions can almost always be recovered. We provide tight bounds on the parameter thresholds for which fixed points in this binarized family are stable, thereby identifying the threshold for binarization in this model, and present numerical evidence that the mean-field model correctly predicts behavioral regimes in certain large random networks, including Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi networks. Moreover, this problem provides a case study in the application of mean-field models, gradient flows, and optimal transport to the study of large-scale systems, and we highlight a number of features of this problem which are informative in this respect.

papers.title: What remains when integrability fails? Mathematical structure in the K(m,m) compacton equations
papers.abstract: Peter Lax's 1968 discovery that certain nonlinear wave equations possess operator pairs (Lax pairs) opened the theory of completely integrable systems, yielding exact solutions, infinite conservation hierarchies, and perfectly elastic soliton collisions. When a nonlinear dispersive equation is provably non-integrable (admitting no Lax pair and only finitely many conservation laws), what mathematical structure governs its dynamics? The K(m,m) compacton equations, u_t + (u^m)_x + (u^m)_{xxx} = 0 for m >= 2, provide a testing ground: they support traveling waves with compact support, yet fail every known integrability test. We prove universal algebraic formulas determining the shape, width, and speed of every K(m,m) compacton. We develop a constraint-deficit mechanism explaining how the five independent conservation laws constrain emergent amplitudes and suppress the fundamental Fourier mode of the collision debris, while higher radiation modes remain unconstrained. The mechanism's conclusions rest on explicit hypotheses supported by numerical evidence. A phase-plane analysis reveals the compacton as a singular limit of smooth solitary waves through simultaneous regularity loss and support compactification. These results delineate intermediate territory between integrable order and generic nonlinear dynamics, organized by scaling universality and by the constraint deficit of a finite conservation structure.

papers.title: Degree growth of rational and meromorphic self-maps
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, or a dominant meromorphic self-map of a compact K\"ahler manifold. We prove that in every codimension, the degree sequence of $f$ differs from its dynamical-degree growth by at most a polynomial factor, with an explicit universal bound on the polynomial exponent. In particular, subexponential but superpolynomial degree growth cannot occur. At a strict dynamical-degree break, we prove the sharper asymptotic \[ \mathrm{deg}_{i,\omega}(f^n)=C_{f,\omega,i}\,\lambda_i(f)^n+O(\eta^n), \] for every $\sqrt{\lambda_{i-1}(f)\lambda_{i+1}(f)}<\eta<\lambda_i(f)$. This extends the degree-asymptotic theorem of Dang--Favre from codimension one in characteristic zero to arbitrary codimension and arbitrary characteristic, and recovers the surface theorem of Boucksom--Favre--Jonsson. Both results rely on a uniform estimate for the temporal discrete logarithmic Laplacian of the degree sequences, obtained by applying the Ptolemy inequality to ordered Hodge--Lorentz packages on varying finite-time orbit spaces.

papers.title: Stability of Diophantine Minimal Foliations in Arbitrary Codimension
papers.abstract: We generalize Moser's stability theorem for minimal hypersurface foliations to arbitrary codimension. Let $\mathbb{T}^N=\mathbb{R}^N/\mathbb{Z}^N$ be the standard torus, and let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be an $m$-plane satisfying a Diophantine condition relative to $\mathbb{Z}^N$. We prove that, under every sufficiently small smooth $\mathbb{Z}^N$-periodic perturbation of the Euclidean metric, the affine foliation of $\mathbb{T}^N$ induced by $P$ persists as a smoothly conjugate foliation by minimal $m$-dimensional submanifolds. The normalized conjugating displacement depends smoothly and tamely on the metric and is locally unique. The proof uses Hamilton's formulation of the Nash-Moser implicit function theorem.

papers.title: On the singular set of the geodesic flow on nonpositively curved surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that the singular locus of the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of a nonpositively curved surface enjoys an additional regularity property: its characteristic function belongs to the geometric anisotropic Sobolev space $H^{5/8-}_xH^{-13/16}_\theta$. In particular, this implies that if the geodesic flow is not ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure, then the zero set of the curvature must be thick in the sense that it supports a nonzero, nonnegative function in $H^{5/8-}$. The proof relies on semiclassical analysis and a new radial estimate for parabolic flows.

papers.title: A Bogomolov property for moduli spaces of polynomials over abelian extensions
papers.abstract: Let $d\geq2$ be an integer, and let $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$ be the moduli space of degree-$d$ polynomials. For every number field $K$, we prove that there exists $\epsilon_{K,d}>0$ such that \[ \left\lbrace\alpha\in\operatorname{MPoly}^d(K^{\mathrm{ab}})\colon h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\alpha)<\epsilon_{K,d}\right\rbrace=\left\lbrace\alpha\in\operatorname{MPoly}^d(K^{\mathrm{ab}})\colon h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\alpha)=0\right\rbrace \] is finite, where $h_{\mathrm{crit}}$ is the critical height. In particular, only finitely many $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$-rational points of $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$ are postcritically finite. The proof combines the correspondence method of Ji--Song--Xie with local ramification estimates and the uniform finiteness of intertwined classes in $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$. We also prove an analogous finiteness theorem for non-preperiodic marked points in non-isotrivial one-parameter polynomial families.

papers.title: Example of exponential many collisions of identical hard disks in the plane
papers.abstract: Let $ \operatorname{MaxCol}(n,d) $ denote the maximal number of nonsimultaneous elastic collisions among $n$ identical hard balls moving freely in $\mathbb{R}^d$. We give a planar construction with exponential lower bound with respect to $n$: $ \operatorname{MaxCol}(n,2)\geq 2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}, \quad n\geq3 $.

papers.title: H\"older regularity for metric Anosov flows
papers.abstract: We define a class of flows on compact metric spaces that we call \emph{$C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flows}, $0 < \alpha < 1$ or $\alpha = \mathrm{Lip}$. We give verifiable criteria for a metric Anosov flow to be $C^\alpha$. We show that $C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flows have H\"older continuous local product structure, and in particular H\"older continuous holonomies. We deduce that topological conjugacies between $C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flows are automatically H\"older continuous. We show that any $C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flow admits a strong (i.e. H\"older continuous) Markov coding. This yields strong ergodic properties for equilibrium states for H\"older potentials for $C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flows. The regularity of the local product structure is proved in a non-compact setting which applies for the geodesic flow on the universal cover of a locally CAT(-1) space. This allows us to obtain H\"older regularity results for the holonomy maps for pinched negative curvature manifolds with respect to the Sasaki metric. This contrasts with the result of Ballmann, Brin and Burns that there are examples in this class for which the dynamical distributions are not H\"older.

papers.title: Survivor Set of Gauss Map with a Hole at $1$
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be the Gauss map. For each $\alpha\in [0,1]$, let $E(\alpha)$ be the survivor set consisting of all $x\in [0,1]$ whose orbit $\{T^k(x):k\ge 0\}$ never enters the interval $(\alpha,1]$. We prove that the set-valued function $\alpha\mapsto E(\alpha)$ is increasing and locally constant almost everywhere. Moreover, we explicitly characterize all intervals where the function $\alpha\mapsto E(\alpha)$ remains constant. We also describe the points at which the map $\alpha\mapsto E(\alpha)$ is not locally constant. Further, we obtain the Hausdorff dimension of $E(\alpha)$ for all $\alpha\in [0,1]$. We prove that the function $\alpha\mapsto \dim_H(E(\alpha))$ forms a devil's staircase on $(0,1]$, but is not continuous at $0$. This discontinuity implies that the result of Raith [Acta Math. Univ. Comenian. 63 (1994), 39-53] fails for piecewise monotone interval maps with infinitely many branches. Finally, we give an application quantifying the set of points sharing identical $\alpha$-continued fraction expansion and regular continued fraction expansion.

papers.title: On the Julia sets of the non-autonomous iteration of exponential maps
papers.abstract: This paper studies non-autonomous iterations of $\lambda e^z$, where at each step the parameter $\lambda$ is chosen from a bounded interval. Urba\'nski and Zdunik introduced and developed a thermodynamic formalism for random dynamics of exponential maps, extending the autonomous result established independently by Rees and Lyubich to typical parameter sequences in $[A, B]^{\mathbb{N}}$ with $1/e<A<B<\infty$. In this paper, we show that the same conclusion indeed holds for all parameters in $[A, B]^{\mathbb{N}}$, Our proof is based on carefully crafted uniform versions of pullback arguments, inspired by the original methods of Rees and Lyubich. In a related direction, Urba\'nski and Zdunik established a non-autonomous analogue of Misiurewicz's theorem for the exponential map, later refined by Lech. We further extend their work by providing a refined condition for the Julia set to be the entire complex plane.

papers.title: Conley Index of Limit Cycles in Filippov Vector Fields
papers.abstract: Within the framework of multivalued dynamical systems, we compute the Conley index for a class of limit cycles in planar Filippov systems. We classify these cycles according to their interaction with the switching manifold, including crossing, sliding, and mixed regimes. Using the Conley index for multivalued admissible maps developed by Mrozek, we construct the appropriate index pairs and determine the corresponding indices for each class. These computations enlarge the class of Filippov invariant sets for which the Conley index is known and extend previous results on low-codimension singularities to periodic dynamics.

papers.title: Stable Manifolds and Uniqueness of Parabolic Rays in the Newtonian $N$-Body Problem
papers.abstract: We study uniqueness for parabolic motions in the Newtonian $N$-body problem with a prescribed minimal normalized central configuration at infinity. A McGehee compactification identifies their tails with the strong stable manifold of the corresponding outgoing zero-energy equilibrium. The configuration projection of this manifold is locally a smooth graph, yielding a smooth initial-velocity field and uniqueness among all parabolic motions confined to a sufficiently narrow truncated cone, without any minimizing assumption. For parabolic geodesic rays, a renormalized action excess and a quantitative no-exit argument remove the confinement hypothesis when the initial configuration lies sufficiently far inside a smaller cone. We then prove that the set of collision-free initial configurations admitting more than one such ray has Lebesgue measure zero. The global argument propagates the local stable manifold backward, discards critical values of the configuration projections by Sard's theorem, and separates distinct regular branches through an explicit differential formula for their renormalized excess. No nondegeneracy assumption on the prescribed minimal central configuration is required. The proofs combine invariant-manifold theory with direct action comparisons and do not use weak KAM theory, Busemann functions, or the differentiability theory of Hamilton--Jacobi solutions.

papers.title: Dynamical Properties of Perturbed Weighted Shifts
papers.abstract: In this paper, sufficient conditions are established for diagonal perturbations of weighted shifts to be supercyclic, hypercyclic, and frequently hypercyclic, extending several classical results for weighted shifts to this more general setting. In addition, a complete analytic characterization of the shadowing property for these operators is obtained. Consequently, examples of frequently hypercyclic perturbed weighted shifts with the shadowing property are constructed.

papers.title: Computation of Attractor Lattices for a Class of Hybrid Systems
papers.abstract: We study the attractor lattice of a class of hybrid dynamical systems on compact metric spaces. Under the trapping guard condition, we prove that hybrid attractors form a bounded distributive lattice isomorphic to the attractor lattice of an associated semiflow. The regularized preimages define a lattice epimorphism from a sublattice of the regular closed, attracting neighborhoods of the semiflow onto those of the hybrid system, and from the whole lattice when the guard set and its reset image have empty interior. Then, using grids on the state space, we construct a convergent cofiltration of outer approximations of a fixed-time map of this semiflow. This construction realizes every finite sublattice of hybrid attractors by a lattice of attracting neighborhoods that are unions of grid elements at sufficiently fine resolutions, and provides index pairs for computing Conley indices. We illustrate these constructions computationally by extracting the Conley--Morse graphs of the bouncing ball, the rimless wheel, the spiking neuron, and exhibiting the attractor lattice for an impacting oscillator.

papers.title: Sparsity and uniformity in dynamical Manin--Mumford problems
papers.abstract: For endomorphisms of the complex projective plane of a given degree, we prove that the existence of a special curve of bounded degree, in the sense of the dynamical Manin--Mumford conjecture, is confined to a proper algebraic subvariety of the parameter space. This confirms a conjecture of DeMarco and Mavraki in dimension two. For general regular polynomial endomorphisms of $\mathbb A^k$, we obtain a uniform dynamical Manin--Mumford bound outside an exceptional hypersurface. These results arise from a common strategy, valid in every dimension and codimension, which reduces such questions to the geometry of exceptional loci in the space of pairs formed by subvarieties and maps. We control these loci by combining arithmetic equidistribution, blender constructions, dynamical directions, monodromy arguments, and degenerations at the boundary of parameter space.

papers.title: Dimension of affine iterated function systems on $\mathbb{R}^d$
papers.abstract: Let $\{f_i(x)=M_ix+a_i\}_{i\in I}$ be an affine iterated function system on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with attractor $\Lambda$, and let $\mu$ be an associated self-affine measure. Assume that the $M_i$ generate a Zariski dense subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb{R})$. Under the strong open set condition, we show that $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\Lambda$ equals the affinity dimension and that $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mu$ equals the Lyapunov dimension. The above results are consequences of the following projection theorem, which requires no separation condition. For every $1\leq n\leq d$ and for Furstenberg measure a.e. $(d-n)$-dimensional subspace $V$, \[ \dim_{\mathrm{H}} (P^V)_*\mu=\min\{n,\,\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mu\}. \] This projection theorem in fact holds under hypotheses weaker than Zariski density: simplicity of the Lyapunov spectrum and a mild transversality condition (the Oseledets non-concentration property). The source of dimension increment in our proof is the positive dimension of the fiberwise conditional measures, exploited through Wu's one-dimensional entropy increase theorem. A key ingredient in reducing the higher-dimensional problem to this setting is a new structural result: a slab-filling property of the measure.

papers.title: Continuum-many discontinuous actions of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on manifolds
papers.abstract: For any $n\geq 1$, we construct a continuum of non-conjugate actions by homeomorphisms of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on the $n$-sphere $S^{n}$ that do not extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{R})$. We do this by adapting a blow-up construction of Bowden and Mann. We motivate studying these actions and note down some related observations.

papers.title: The entry-exit function and nilpotent corrections in multidimensional slow-fast systems
papers.abstract: We study multidimensional entry-exit phenomena in slow-fast systems whose fast linearization contains a nilpotent component. We show that the classical spectral balance still determines the exit point as $\varepsilon \to 0$, however the nilpotent component induces an algebraic amplification invisible to the spectrum, producing a $\varepsilon|\log\varepsilon|$-shift of the exit point for $0 <\varepsilon \ll 1$. We further extend the analysis to systems with several spectral branches and show that mode dominance follows a hierarchical, lexicographic selection principle: accumulated spectral growth determines the leading order, while the nilpotent component resolves degeneracies between spectrally equivalent modes.

papers.title: **Winding number forces universal synchronisation**
papers.abstract: We prove that two completely different oscillators synchronise through arbitrarily weak reciprocal impulses. Any two planar oscillators with hyperbolic attracting limit cycles and equal natural periods lock stably one-to-one under translation impulses with generic directions and a suitable range of positive strength ratios, whatever their vector fields, limit cycles and transverse contraction rates. The mechanism is topological: the winding of the asymptotic phase gradient forces phase advances and delays, and the relative winding number of an effective impulse field gives lower bounds on attracting and unstable locked states. Equal periods are not essential: locking persists under small nonzero mismatches, with persistence and loss governed by a shifted phase balance. The analysis covers the full state-dependent impulsive dynamics, including transverse stability. Nearly simultaneous emissions may make the return discontinuous; under an explicit regularity condition the global return has a normally attracting Lipschitz invariant circle with topologically Morse--Smale dynamics.

papers.title: A Smooth Autonomous Flow with Exponential Mixing on the Three-Torus
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth autonomous divergence-free vector field on $\mathbb{T}^3$ whose flow is exponentially mixing with respect to Lebesgue measure. This answers an open question about smooth autonomous exponential mixing in three dimensions. Starting from an exponentially mixing Anosov suspension flow, we perform surgery near four periodic orbits and show that the resulting manifold is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{T}^3$. The resulting vector field has exactly sixteen hyperbolic equilibria. We also prove a general transfer theorem that preserves exponential mixing under certain singular changes of coordinates.

papers.title: Multivariate stable mixing local limit theorem for intermittent diffeomorphisms and flows
papers.abstract: We prove mixing local limit theorems for dynamical systems in the superdiffusive regime where there is convergence to a multivariate stable law (including the nonstandard domain of the central limit theorem). We apply our results to d-dimensional observables for intermittent maps and solenoids, as well as intermittent semiflows and flows.

papers.title: Translational tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets
papers.abstract: The periodic tiling conjecture asserts that if a bounded set $\Omega\subset \mathbb R^d$ of finite measure tiles $\mathbb R^d$ by translations, then it admits at least one fully periodic tiling. This conjecture was proved to hold in $\mathbb R$ by Lagarias and Wang, and was recently disproved by Greenfeld and Tao in sufficiently high dimensions. Its discrete analogue in $\mathbb Z^2$ was proved by Bhattacharya, whereas the conjecture in $\mathbb R^2$ remains open. In this paper, we analyze the structure of tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets: bounded open sets in $\mathbb R^2$ whose boundary is a finite union of line segments parallel to the axes. We prove that every such tiling that is topologically minimal is weakly periodic. Moreover, we show that if an axis-parallel polygonal set $\Omega$ tiles $\mathbb{R}^2$ then it admits a quasi-periodic tiling (i.e., a finite union of translated lattices). The proofs combine geometric decompositions of tilings with rational approximation and discrete tiling theory. As a consequence, we obtain that the translational tiling problem for axis-parallel polygonal sets with real algebraic vertex coordinates is decidable.
